articles.title: Saliba out for ‘extended period’ after back injury for France at World Cup
articles.summary: Saliba went off in the 30th minute of France's World Cup defeat to Spain
articles.content:
Saliba out for ‘extended period’ after back injury for France at World Cup

Saliba went off in the 30th minute of France's World Cup defeat to Spain

Last Update:

Arsenal say defender William Saliba will be out for an “extended period” after a back injury at the World Cup for France.

The centre-back will not require surgery on an injury which saw him substituted in the 30th minute of France’s semi-final defeat tp Spain, but is likely to miss a significant part of Arsenal’s Premier League title defence.

Saliba was one of the standout performers in the Gunners’ title-winning campaign last season, making 50 appearances in all competitions.

Arsenal kick off their 2026-27 campaign against Manchester City in the Community Shield on Sunday, August 16, before the Gunners begin the Premier League season against Coventry five days later.

An Arsenal statement said: “William Saliba has returned to us from World Cup duty, where he played an integral role in France reaching the semi-finals of the competition.

“Subsequent specialist reviews on William’s return to London this week have confirmed that he has suffered a back injury which will require a period of rehabilitation.

“Extensive assessments have concluded that surgery is not recommended, but William should now commence a managed recovery programme.

“William’s rehabilitation will commence immediately, with continual management of his injury, and he is expected to be out of action for an extended period.

“Everyone is fully focused on supporting William to ensure he is back to full fitness as soon as possible.”

Saliba injury: Do Arsenal need a new centre-back?

Arsenal already knew they would be without their main centre-back for a period, but news of the length of that absence will almost certainly see them step up their search for a new defender.

Ezri Konsa and unattached John Stones have both been mentioned as potential targets, with a bid of £30million reportedly rejected by Aston Villa for the former.

Villa are likely to demand much more for the England international, which could make Stones a more viable option, albeit questions remain over the former Manchester City man’s fitness.

The 32-year-old played five times for the Three Lions at the World Cup, including every minute of the quarter-final and semi-final, but he started only five times for City in the Premier League last term.

articles.title: Revealed: Five attackers Arsenal could target after missing out on Morgan Rogers
articles.summary: Arsenal are in need of a new left-sided forward after being snubbed by Rogers
articles.content:
Revealed: Five attackers Arsenal could target after missing out on Morgan Rogers

Arsenal are in need of a new left-sided forward after being snubbed by Rogers

Last Update:

After weeks and even months linking Arsenal with Morgan Rogers, the England forward will be lining up in the blue of Chelsea next season in what is a huge blow for the Premier League champions.

The Blues stole in ahead of their London rivals to land Rogers from Aston Villa for a British-record £117million, forcing Mikel Arteta and Co to look elsewhere in their pursuit of a new left-sided attacker.

Christian Tzolis’ impending arrival has helped to plug the gap left by Leandro Trossard but with Gabriel Martinelli also linked with the exit door, Arteta will be keen to add another quality attacking addition to ensure they remain among Europe’s top teams.

articles.title: Casemiro’s next club revealed after leaving Manchester United – but league opens investigation into tampering claims
articles.summary: Casemiro left Manchester United after four years this summer
articles.content:
Casemiro’s next club revealed after leaving Manchester United – but league opens investigation into tampering claims

Casemiro left Manchester United after four years this summer

Last Update:

Casemiro has joined Major League Soccer side Inter Miami following his departure from Manchester United.

The Brazilian midfielder left the Red Devils upon the expiry of his contract on June 30, ending a four-year spell at Old Trafford which saw him make 111 Premier League appearances and lift the FA Cup and Carabao Cup.

Having just returned from representing Brazil at the World Cup, the ex-Real Madrid star has now opted for a switch to MLS, where he will link up with Lionel Messi in the United States.

The former Manchester United star was officially unveiled by Miami on Wednesday after agreeing a deal through to the end of the 2027 MLS season, with the option to extend his stay until June 2029.

Casemiro joins Inter Miami.. but MLS investigate transfer

However, shortly after confirming the transfer, MLS released a statement revealing it had opened a review into a potential breach of league rules.

“The league is gathering all relevant information and will refrain from further comment until the review is complete,” the statement read.

MLS also confirmed that although Inter Miami and LA Galaxy had reached an agreement over Casemiro’s discovery rights, the details of that arrangement would not be disclosed until the investigation had concluded.

The probe centres on MLS’ discovery rights system, which allows clubs to claim priority over players who are not currently in the league.

Each MLS side can place up to five players on its discovery list at any one time, giving them the first opportunity to negotiate if one of those players decides to move to the United States.

LA Galaxy held Casemiro’s discovery rights before Inter Miami completed a deal to acquire them, paving the way for the experienced midfielder’s arrival in Florida.

articles.title: Aston Villa agree loan deal for Chelsea flop following Rogers’ deal
articles.summary: He is set to join after a disappointing spell in west London.
articles.content:
Aston Villa agree loan deal for Chelsea flop following Rogers’ deal

He is set to join after a disappointing spell in west London.

Last Update:

Aston Villa have agreed to sign Alejandro Garnacho on an initial loan deal from Chelsea.

According to multiple reports, the two Premier League clubs have reached an agreement on a temporary deal that will become permanent if certain conditions are met.

Should the deal be made permanent, the 22-year-old will sign a four-year contract at Villa Park.

The news comes after Chelsea confirmed the signing of England attacking midfielder Morgan Rogers from Villa in a deal worth £117million, a record for a British player.

Garnacho’s arrival represents a gamble by Villa, whose squad has already changed significantly from the one that won the Europa League and finished fourth in the Premier League last season, securing a return to the Champions League.

In addition to Rogers, star midfielder Youri Tielemans departed for Manchester United, with Villa bringing in midfielder Joao Gomes and Switzerland World Cup star Johan Manzambi.

Garnacho, a Copa America winner in 2024, was not at the World Cup, having endured an underwhelming season with Chelsea following his move from Manchester United.

He scored just one goal and provided four assists in 24 Premier League appearances as the Blues limped to a 10th-place finish. Garnacho scored eight goals across all competitions.

However, Villa boss Unai Emery seemingly believes he can get the best out of Garnacho. For a side looking to continue on an upward trajectory after losing their prized asset, it is very important he is proven correct.

articles.title: Valverde hails ‘special person’ Mourinho as Real Madrid captain targets end to trophy drought
articles.summary: Skipper Valverde returned to training on Wednesday and had praise for the new Real Madrid boss.
articles.content:
Valverde hails ‘special person’ Mourinho as Real Madrid captain targets end to trophy drought

Skipper Valverde returned to training on Wednesday and had praise for the new Real Madrid boss.

Last Update:

Federico Valverde labelled Jose Mourinho as a “special person” as he stressed his desire to ensure the first season of the Real Madrid coach’s second spell in charge is one that results in trophies.

Valverde returned to Madrid’s training base for his first session under Mourinho on Wednesday.

The Madrid captain endured a disappointing World Cup with Uruguay as they crashed out in the group stage, failing to win any of their three games against Saudi Arabia, Cape Verde and eventual champions Spain.

But he is now firmly focused on the goal of adding to his tally of 14 trophies with Madrid, who suffered the rare ignominy of a trophy-less season last term in a tumultuous campaign that saw Valverde injured in a training ground bust-up with Aurelien Tchouameni in its closing stages.

Mourinho’s appointment as the successor to Alvaro Arbeloa raised eyebrows, but Valverde expressed excitement at the chance to play under the man who helped Madrid dethrone Pep Guardiola’s Barcelona in LaLiga in 2011-12.

“I’m really looking forward to learning from him, listening to every piece of advice he offers, and making the most of every second and minute of training I get to share with him and his coaching staff,” Valverde told Real Madrid TV.

“I want to learn and grow as both a person and a footballer. He is a special person I can learn a great deal from. I hope it’s a wonderful season.”

On his captaincy, Valverde added: “I feel a great sense of excitement and honour. Whenever someone on the street or within my circle mentions it, it truly fills me with pride and emotion.

“You reflect on everything that has happened — the good times and the bad — and now the moment has arrived for me to be the first captain. I learned so much from all the team-mates who served as captains here. They always offered incredible support, and I intend to build on that experience to grow alongside the coaching staff.

“This is the year I want to truly enjoy the game and give my absolute all—not just on the pitch, but off it as well—to ensure all my team-mates feel comfortable.

“It’s not just me; the whole team feels it. What we want most is to win trophies this year, to make the Madridistas happy so they can enjoy a season full of silverware and feel proud of us.”

Madrid will play their first unofficial game of Mourinho’s second spell when they face Albacete, who knocked Los Blancos out of the Copa del Rey last season, a week on Friday.

articles.title: ‘Worth as much as the gold medal’ – Yamal reveals Messi message after Spain’s World Cup triumph over Argentina
articles.summary: Messi had words of wisdom for the man seen as his successor.
articles.content:
‘Worth as much as the gold medal’ – Yamal reveals Messi message after Spain’s World Cup triumph over Argentina

Messi had words of wisdom for the man seen as his successor.

Last Update:

Lamine Yamal revealed the words of advice he received from Lionel Messi following Spain‘s win over Argentina in last Sunday’s World Cup final.

Spain lifted the trophy for the second time in their history after an uninspiring final was settled by Ferran Torres’ extra-time strike.

Ugly scenes followed at the end, with several Spain players accosted by Argentina counterparts. Leandro Paredes was at the centre of the controversy, as he grabbed Eric Garcia by the throat before pushing Gavi to the turf. Paredes could yet face disciplinary action for his conduct, however, with FIFA set to open an investigation into his behaviour.

But there was sportsmanship on show between Argentina legend Messi and Yamal, seen as the man to assume his mantle at Barcelona after a phenomenal start to his club career.

The pair embraced on the pitch after the full-time whistle and, speaking to Marca, Yamal disclosed the motivational message Messi gave to the 19-year-old.

“He’s the greatest player in history and someone I’ve always looked up to,” Yamal said. “After the match, I wanted to show him my respect.

“He told me to keep following my path and that the future belongs to our generation.

“Those words are worth as much as the gold medal hanging around my neck.”

Yamal scored only one goal at the World Cup, which came in the group stage win over Saudi Arabia, and did not register an assist.

However, Yamal still had a great influence on Spain’s success with his undoubted physical ability and flair, completing more dribbles (35) than any other player at the tournament.

Having become the joint-fourth youngest player to win the World Cup at 19 years and six days, Yamal will be expected to be at the forefront of La Roja’s efforts to defend the European Championship in 2028 and the World Cup two years later, when the tournament will be co-hosted by Spain.

articles.title: Italy: ‘Exceptions’ being made to try to lure Guardiola to Azzurri job
articles.summary: Italy are attempting to convince Pep Guardiola to make his first foray into international coaching.
articles.content:
Italy: ‘Exceptions’ being made to try to lure Guardiola to Azzurri job

Italy are attempting to convince Pep Guardiola to make his first foray into international coaching.

Last Update:

Pep Guardiola is in talks about becoming the next Italy coach, with the president of the Italian Football Federation (FIGC) revealing that financial “exceptions” are being made to try to secure a deal.

Guardiola brought the curtain down on a 10-year spell as Manchester City manager in May.

The former Barcelona and Bayern Munich boss has never managed a national team, though he reportedly had an agreement with England in 2024 before changing his mind.

Italy are looking for a new coach after missing out on a third successive World Cup, the Azzurri failing to qualify for the 2026 tournament after losing a play-off final to Bosnia-Herzegovina on penalties.

Another former City manager, Roberto Mancini, is also in the running. Mancini led Italy to glory in Euro 2020. Meanwhile, former Italy midfielder Andrea Pirlo is under consideration despite his coaching career, which has seen spells with Juventus and Sampdoria, featuring little success to this point.

Guardiola is the standout name, but FIGC president Giovanni Malago stressed that him succeeding Gennaro Gattuso is no guarantee.

Malago told Cronache di Spogliatoio: “It’s not a given that this will come to fruition, but I believe it was right and important to open a dialogue and keep it alive.

“This [talks with Guardiola] is by no means a lack of respect towards other candidates, with whom discussions have already begun, and adding another name would in no way detract from the process.

“There are also financial and budgetary considerations. In the short to medium term, to say that we’ll have to tighten our belts is an understatement. However, some exceptions have been made, which may relate to the name that is so dominant at the moment: Pep Guardiola.”

Asked if Guardiola, Mancini and Pirlo are the only candidates for the vacant role, Malago replied: “Absolutely not. We think about a certain profile and certainly these names fall into that category.”

Having watched Spain win the 2026 World Cup from afar, Italy will return to action in September when they face Belgium in the UEFA Nations League. The Azzurri have been drawn in a difficult group that also features France and Turkey.

articles.title: Disgraced Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes set to play for Boca Juniors tomorrow night
articles.summary: Leandro Paredes has shunned a post-World Cup break and is set to return to action for Boca Juniors on Thursday night
articles.content:
Disgraced Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes set to play for Boca Juniors tomorrow night

Leandro Paredes has shunned a post-World Cup break and is set to return to action for Boca Juniors on Thursday night

Last Update:

Leandro Paredes is poised to play for Boca Juniors on Thursday night, just four days after appearing in the World Cup final.

The Argentina midfielder came on at half-time in Sunday’s 1-0 defeat to Spain in New Jersey, playing 75 minutes as the game went to extra-time.

Paredes received widespread criticism after being involved in the disgraceful scenes at the final whistle that saw several Spain players physically assaulted by Argentines. Paredes was at the centre of the controversy, grabbing Eric Garcia by the throat before pushing Gavi to the turf.

It was widely reported that the 32-year-old had been sent-off for his actions but it later came to light that no action had been taken by referee Slavko Vincic. Paredes is still likely to face a sanction, though, with FIFA set to open an investigation into Argentina’s conduct.

The former PSG, Juventus and Roma man took to Instagram the day after the game but offered no apology.

He wrote: “Thank you Argentina! I love you today, and always.

“Today, I write with a heavy heart, having been unable to bring our country the joy it so richly deserves – but with a chest full of pride for having given everything we had and for flying our flag at the very top once again.

“Thank you to everyone who was part of this national team – to this group of players who gave their all to represent this jersey, fighting for it until the very last second of every match.

“It was an honour to be part of the best Argentine national team in history.”

Paredes trains with Boca

Having flown back to Argentina on Monday and joined in the celebrations that greeted the team’s return, Paredes immediately linked back up with the Boca squad at their Buenos Aires training complex.

Paredes was filmed working out in the gym and training with his team-mates ahead of the Copa Sudamericana clash with Chilean side O’Higgins at La Bombonera.

The Boca skipper has been named in the squad and is expected to start on the bench despite sustaining a minor rib injury during the World Cup.

articles.title: Donald Trump ready to endorse Gianni Infantino for the role of secretary-general of the United Nations
articles.summary: Donald Trump and Gianni Infantino struck up a close bond during the 2026 World Cup and the US president wants the FIFA chief to take on a more significant role
articles.content:
Donald Trump ready to endorse Gianni Infantino for the role of secretary-general of the United Nations

Donald Trump and Gianni Infantino struck up a close bond during the 2026 World Cup and the US president wants the FIFA chief to take on a more significant role

Last Update:

Donald Trump would like FIFA chief Gianni Infantino to become the next secretary-general of the United Nations.

Trump and Infantino have developed a close bond after working together to help the US deliver a successful World Cup, alongside Canada and Mexico, and the US president would like to see him play a greater role in politics moving forward.

According the New York Post, Infantino would be Trump’s preferred candidate to replace Antonio Guterres when the Portuguese steps down in December.

A source close to the president told the Post: “He [Infantino] is respected by everyone around the world, and [Trump] recognises he has a special ability to bring people together.”

Infantino, who awarded Trump FIFA’s inaugural Peace Prize in December, is thought to be happy in his current role and the reported £4.5million annual salary. But if he does throw his name into the hat to replace Guterres he would have to receive the endorsement of the 15-member UN Security Council and then the confirmation of the General Assembly.

Table of Contents

Infantino’s record shows he knows how to manage – US special envoy

Paolo Zampolli, Trump’s special envoy for global partnerships, told the Post: “Only President Trump could have such a genius idea.

“At the United Nations, you have to deal with 193 member states. In FIFA, there are over 200 members [and] Gianni’s great record shows he knows how to manage.”

Trump has been a frequent critic of the United Nations since returning for a second term as president and often voiced his frutration at their lack of intervention in global conflicts.

The Post speculates that having Infantino in a senior role at the UN would improve its relationship with the US.

Infantino continues to divide world football

Infantino remains a divisive figure in the world of football. While many confederations like the idea of an expanded World Cup that this year saw a record 48 teams take part, that view is not shared by many in Europe, who believe it dilutes the quality of the product.

The issue of hydration breaks also drew criticism, as did the extended half-time break in the final to allow the likes of Madonna, Justin Bieber and Shakira to perform.

Infantino was accused of fawning to Trump during the tournament when a conversation between the two led to the suspension of a red card awarded to USA striker Folarin Balogun in the round of 32 clash with Bosnia and Herzegovina.

Balogun was allowed to play in the subsequent game with Belgium but couldn’t prevent his side from losing 4-1.

articles.title: Morgan Rogers completes £117m Chelsea transfer as Arsenal miss out on Aston Villa midfielder
articles.summary: Chelsea have signed England midfielder Morgan Rogers from Villa
articles.content:
Morgan Rogers completes £117m Chelsea transfer as Arsenal miss out on Aston Villa midfielder

Chelsea have signed England midfielder Morgan Rogers from Villa

Last Update:

Chelsea have signed Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa for £117m on a six-year deal after the England midfielder reportedly turned down Arsenal to work with new Blues head coach Xabi Alonso.

The Midlands club confirmed their star man’s departure in a statement on social media, saying: “Aston Villa can confirm that Morgan Rogers has completed a permanent transfer to Chelsea.

“Since joining from Middlesbrough in 2024, the midfielder has enjoyed a rapid rise to prominence, helping Villa to lift the UEFA Europa League last term, scoring the third goal in the final in Istanbul.

“During his time at the club, he also earned his first senior England caps, representing his country at the FIFA World Cup 2026, where the Three Lions finished third.

“A player with impeccable behaviour and commitment, Morgan leaves Aston Villa with the best wishes of everyone at the football club for both his service to the club and for his future career. He will always remain a core part of our recent great moments and memories.”

Speaking for the first time as a Chelsea player, Rogers added: “I’m so excited; for me, Chelsea are the biggest club in London and a club I’ve always admired since I was a kid.

“I’m really excited about the project with the new manager, the players we’ve got and where the club is heading. That’s why I’m here and I can’t wait to get started.”

Table of Contents

Morgan Rogers stats: Aston Villa, Middlesbrough

Born in Halesowen in the West Midlands, Rogers spent nine years at nearby West Bromwich Albion’s academy before joining Manchester City, winning the 2019/20 FA Youth Cup.

He had loan spells with Lincoln City, Bournemouth and Blackpool and then joined Middlesbrough permanently, scoring seven goals to help Boro finish eighth in the Championship and reach the EFL Cup semi-finals in 2023/24.

Villa signed Rogers for an initial £8 million in February 2024 and he swiftly established himself as an important figure for Unai Emery’s team, proceeding to contribute 14 goals and 15 assists across all competitions in 2024/25, including a hat-trick in a Champions League victory against Celtic.

Those numbers earned Rogers the Villa and PFA Young Player of the Year honours, and he added 14 goals and 11 assists in 2025/26, winning the Europa League Player of the Season award as Villa lifted the trophy.

No English player bettered Rogers’ total of 84 attempts at goal in the 2025/26 Premier League, while no midfielder eclipsed his tally of 32 on target.

His goals-vs-expected-goals total of 3.22 was also the eighth-highest of any player in the division, helped by Rogers’ talent for spectacular strikes.

Morgan Rogers England career: World Cup starter

An England regular at youth level between the ages of 14 and 21, Rogers made his senior debut away to Greece in the Nations League in November 2024.

Lee Carsley, who was interim England head coach following Gareth Southgate’s exit, gave Rogers his bow and current boss Thomas Tuchel has continued to pick him since becoming Southgate’s permanent successor at the start of 2025.

Rogers scored his only Three Lions goal in a 3-0 friendly win at home to Wales in October 2025 and was called up for the World Cup 2026, appearing in seven of England’s eight matches at the finals.

A full World Cup debutant against Panama during the group stage, Rogers played throughout England’s semi-final defeat to Argentina – crossing for Anthony Gordon to open the scoring – and third-place play-off win over France.

When does Chelsea’s Premier League 2026/27 season start?

Chelsea’s Premier League season begins away to Fulham on Monday, August 24 at 20:00 BST.

In the UK, the game will be shown live on Sky Sports Main Event, Premier League and Ultra, with streaming via Sky Go.

articles.title: Premier League: The ONE player your club should sign this summer
articles.summary: Nico Williams is one player we would love to see in the Premier League next season but who should sign him?
articles.content:
Premier League: The ONE player your club should sign this summer

Nico Williams is one player we would love to see in the Premier League next season but who should sign him?

Last Update:

The World Cup is over and the wait for the domestic game to return is now underway.

The EFL re-starts on Friday, August 14 and the Premier League a week later when champions Arsenal host newly promoted Coventry.

Between now and then there is bound to be frantic transfer activity as clubs attempt to bolster their squads before the big kick-off.

Here, we identify one signing that each club should make in the summer window.

Table of Contents

ARSENAL

With Morgan Rogers seemingly heading for Chelsea, sporting director Andrea Berta will have to train his focus elsewhere. The sale of Leandro Trossard now appears slightly misjudged and the Gunners will surely be in the market for a winger. Nico Williams endured an injury-interrupted season with Athletic Bilbao in 2025/26 but showed his quality off the bench in the World Cup final. Has a release clause of around £80million which would not be a problem. If he can stay fit, the 24-year-old would be tailor-made for the Premier League.Target: Nico Williams

ASTON VILLA

It is another busy summer at Villa Park as the club try to move forward while complying with financial regulations. Rogers’ departure is a blow, albeit one softened slightly by the arrivals of Joao Gomes and Johan Manzambi. Villa are reportedly willing to let Ollie Watkins go but that would leave them desperately short of striking options. Nicolas Jackson would be the ideal replacement. The 25-year-old Senegal international needs to feel loved after two largely underwhelming seasons at Chelsea and Bayern Munich and, if he does, he could help fire Villa to a top-four finish.Target: Nicolas Jackson

BOURNEMOUTH

The Cherries need defenders following the departures of Marcos Senesi and Alex Jimenez. Aaron Wan-Bissaka is not the kind of up-and-coming player Bournemouth normally target but he would be a very solid, relatively low-cost option from relegated West Ham.Target: Aaron Wan-Bissaka

BRENTFORD

Brentford have made a couple of eye-catching moves this summer, but only because they have a different profile from the kind of player they usual go for. Bringing in Jaidon Anthony from Burnley was a surprise move but not as shocking as signing 34-year-old Callum Wilson from West Ham. Cologne winger Said El Mala was linked earlier in the summer and his signing would be a real coup with Borussia Dortmund also interested.Target: Said El Mala

BRIGHTON

Brighton’s famed algorithm reportedly led to them agreeing terms with El Mala in April, although they are said to have disagreed with Cologne over his value and the 19-year-old Germany youth winger has joined pre-season training with the Bundesliga club. Albion will perhaps look to add more experience following the departures of James Milner, Joel Veltman, Solly March and coach Andrew Crofts, with John Stones a dream signing for fans but likely too much of a coup right now. Finding a forward as prolific and classy as Danny Welbeck looks as urgent as ever with a potentially long European campaign expanding the schedule. The answer could come from within the squad, with Georginio Rutter a work in progress in the Premier League and prospects Charalampos Kostoulas and Stefanos Tzimas hoping to prove themselves.Target: Said El Mala

CHELSEA

Chelsea’s endless spending shows no sign of slowing down with Rogers set to join Marco Palestra and Geovany Quenda at Stamford Bridge this summer. Chelsea were also interested in Granit Xhaka before Sunderland ruled out any chance of their captain leaving Wearside. With Chelsea’s owners promising to bring in ‘Premier League-ready’ players this summer, new boss Xabi Alonso would love some older heads. England international Stones would be a perfect fit in a defence that often creaked last season.Target: John Stones

COVENTRY CITY

Coventry must recruit heavily and recruit well. The formula on how to stay in the Premier League following promotion was outlined by Sunderland and Leeds last season with both clubs surviving with ease. An obvious position they need to recruit in is goalkeeper with the on-loan Carl Rushworth returning to parent club Brighton after playing a key role in their Championship title success. Reports suggest the 25-year-old is desperate to rejoin the Sky Blues and this seems a no-brainer for boss Frank Lampard.Target: Carl Rushworth

CRYSTAL PALACE

Palace have had some high-profile departures in recent years – Michael Olise and Eberechi Eze, for example – and it seems Maxence Lacroix could well join them with Chelsea sniffing round the France international. If Lacroix does leave Selhurst Park then Palace will need a commanding central defender to fill the void. Chelsea have reportedly made Trevoh Chalobah available for transfer. The former Palace loanee would be an ideal fit.Target: Trevoh Chalobah

EVERTON

Everton are a classic David Moyes team; honest, workmanlike but lacking in star quality. Jack Grealish brought it in the first half of last season before injury struck. A permanent deal to bring Grealish back to the Hill Dickinson Stadium is a possibility but Everton may be better looking at his Manchester City team-mate Savinho. Blessed with more pace, the Brazilian would immediately bolster Everton’s attacking options, albeit he wouldn’t come cheap.Target: Savinho

FULHAM

One of the most intriguing appointments of the summer was Alvaro Arbeloa’s at Fulham. The former Spain international did not have the most successful spell in charge of Real Madrid last season but was not helped by a dressing room riddled with cliques and in-fighting. Arbeloa is reportedly eager to bring one of Madrid’s starlets with him to Craven Cottage and Gonzalo Garcia would be a shrewd acquisition to replace Raul Jimenez who has rejoined Wolves.Target: Gonzalo Garcia

HULL CITY

Hull are an even more exaggerated version of Coventry. They need a better quality of player in multiple positions although their spending power is likely to be restricted by financial regulations. Free agents and loan moves could be the order of the day and one eye-catching name that has been mentioned is Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Renato Sanches, whose career is in need of rebuilding after he burst on to the scene as a teenager.Target: Renato Sanches

IPSWICH TOWN

Ipswich recruited heavily the last time they were promoted but targeted top-end Championship players in a policy that ultimately failed. The pursuit of centre-half Issa Diop from Fulham suggests they may have learned their lesson but the Morocco centre-half will need to be accompanied by several more experienced Premier League players if they are to survive. New boss Gary O’Neill could do worse than to return to his old club Wolves and snap up Brazil international midfielder Andre, even though he has recently signed a new deal at Molineux.Target: Andre

LEEDS UNITED

Leeds have already signed Harry Wilson and Bosnia and Herzegovina defender Tarik Muharemovic this summer as they look to build on their encouraging return to the top flight last season. The departures of Illan Meslier and Karl Darlow mean they require a goalkeeper. Lucas Perri was hit and miss in his first year at Elland Road and boss Daniel Farke must decide whether to place his faith in the 28-year-old or dip into the market. James Trafford endured a frustrating season at Manchester City last year and could be tempted to make the short move across the M62.Target: James Trafford

LIVERPOOL

Liverpool will hope the arrival of Andoni Iraola will spark an upturn in fortunes following the exit of Arne Slot. Iraola inherits a strong squad but one that needs tweaking. Left-wing has repeatedly been flagged as a position that requires strengthening but with Cody Gakpo, Hugo Ekitike and Florian Wirtz all capable of playing there – not to mention burgeoning talent Rio Ngumoha – there seems little need to invest. Liverpool were often overrun in midfield last season and it may be Iraola returns to his former club Bournemouth in a bid to sign Alex Scott, who has turned down a new contract with the Cherries.Target: Alex Scott

MANCHESTER CITY

City continue to spend while the football world awaits the verdict from an independent commission into allegations the club breached multiple financial rules. Elliot Anderson is the latest big-money arrival, joining from Nottingham Forest for £116m. It’s hard to pick any holes in the City squad but, if there is one area of possible weakness, it is at centre-half with John Stones and Nathan Ake both leaving. City like to sign young players and bring them on which is why Crystal Palace’s Jaydee Canvot, 19, would be the perfect project.Target: Jaydee Canvot

MANCHESTER UNITED

United have been active since the window opened, bringing in midfielders Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans. Their squad has a nice balance to it, although they are still lacking at right-back with Diego Dalot their only senior option. United could do a lot worse than try to prise Ben White from Arsenal, although William Saliba’s back injury could complicate matters.Target: Ben White

NEWCASTLE UNITED

After the departures of Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali, it is imperative Newcastle keep hold of captain Bruno Guimaraes. If the Brazilian leaves for Arsenal then it will open up a huge hole in midfield. A new transfer model that targets younger players has been implemented this summer but Newcastle still need some experience in the middle of the park. He may not be a flashy option but Christian Norgaard was one of the better holding midfielders in the Premier League while at Brentford. Given his limited playing time at Arsenal, he would likely relish a move to the North East.Target: Christian Norgaard

NOTTINGHAM FOREST

Having lost Anderson to City, Forest are in need of a strong central midfielder to plug the gap. Liverpool’s Curtis Jones could be the ideal replacement. The 25-year-old was expected to join Inter Milan but a disagreement over the fee has seen the move thrown into doubt. Forest could, and should, step in. Jones has a similar profile to Anderson and would also give Forest money to play with.Target: Curtis Jones

SUNDERLAND

One of the stories of last season was Sunderland’s remarkable seventh-placed finish just a year after promotion via the play-offs. The challenge now is to build on that success and cope with the additional fixtures thrown up by playing in the Europa League. Sunderland are known to be looking for a left-footed right winger and one name is consistently mentioned: Amad Diallo. The Ivory Coast star had a hugely successful loan spell on Wearside in the 2022/23 season and remains a popular figure at the Stadium of Light. He won’t come cheap with Manchester United eager to retain Diallo but his signing would be a real statement of intent.Target: Amad Diallo

TOTTENHAM

Spurs have been the most active team in the window so far as they look to improve on two successive 17th-placed finishes. They appear certain to better that record next season under Roberto De Zerbi, who has already signed the likes of Andy Robertson, Marcos Senesi, Tonali and Mateus Fernandes. The squad still requires a reliable goalscorer, though, and Bournemouth’s Eli Kroupi Jr has been mentioned as a potential target. The gifted 20-year-old was hugely impressive at the Vitality Stadium last season and would form a major piece of the De Zerbi jigsaw.Target: Eli Kroupi Jr

articles.title: UEFA boss boycotts World Cup final in protest against FIFA
articles.summary: UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin did not attend Sunday's World Cup final.
articles.content:
UEFA boss boycotts World Cup final in protest against FIFA

UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin did not attend Sunday's World Cup final.

Last Update:

UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin did not attend Sunday’s World Cup final between Argentina and Spain in protest against FIFA.

Although Ceferin travelled to Mexico City for the tournament’s opening match between co-hosts Mexico and South Africa, he opted not to attend the final in New Jersey following a series of disagreements with world football’s governing body.

One of the main reasons behind his decision was FIFA’s controversial move to overturn Folarin Balogun’s suspension after intervention from United States President Donald Trump.

UEFA strongly criticised the decision at the time, describing it as “unprecedented, incomprehensible and unjustifiable”.

“When the certainty of rules is no longer guaranteed by its guardians, the integrity of the game is at stake and the credibility of a competition is undermined,” UEFA said in a statement.

Ceferin is also opposed to several other initiatives introduced by FIFA president Gianni Infantino, including the introduction of half-time entertainment shows.

UEFA rejects half-time shows

The World Cup final featured performances from Madonna, BTS, Shakira and Justin Bieber, extending the traditional 15-minute interval to more than 27 minutes.

UEFA has no plans to introduce similar shows at the Champions League or European Championship.

The governing body also remains firmly against proposals to expand the World Cup to 64 teams, an idea Infantino suggested could be explored during the tournament.

Elsewhere, UEFA responded after Somali referee Omar Artan was denied entry to the United States before the World Cup by appointing him to officiate the UEFA Super Cup between Paris Saint-Germain and Aston Villa on August 12.

Ticket pricing has also been a point of disagreement. UEFA intends to broadly freeze prices for Euro 2028, allowing supporters to buy five match tickets for roughly the cost of a single parking space at a World Cup venue in the United States.

articles.summary: Manchester United have completed another piece of clever business this summer.
articles.content:
Manchester United sign highly-rated winger Thompson from Tottenham

Manchester United have completed another piece of clever business this summer.

Last Update:

Manchester United have completed the signing of highly rated winger Tynan Thompson from Tottenham in a deal worth an initial £4 million, with a further £4 million payable in performance-related add-ons.

The 18-year-old joins Old Trafford after emerging as one of Tottenham’s brightest academy prospects and has been promised opportunities to challenge for a place in United’s first-team squad.

Thompson joined Spurs’ academy at the age of 12 and enjoyed an impressive campaign last season, scoring 13 goals and providing six assists across Under-18 and Under-21 level.

Seven of those goals came in seven UEFA Youth League appearances, while his performances also earned him two places on Tottenham’s Champions League matchday bench.

The agreement also includes a 15% sell-on clause in Tottenham’s favour, with the additional payments linked to Thompson’s achievements at first-team level for United.

Confirming the transfer, United said in a statement: “Manchester United have agreed the signing of exciting young winger Tynan Thompson, subject to registration. The England youth international has joined from Tottenham Hotspur.

“The 18-year-old scored 13 goals and contributed six assists last season across Under-18 and Under-21 level, including seven goals in seven UEFA Youth League games. His performances earned him opportunities within Spurs’ first-team matchday squads.

“Everyone at United would like to welcome Tynan to the club and wish him the very best of luck for the future.”

articles.title: Lionel Messi: Time to leave the international scene but remember the good times, not the shame of New Jersey
articles.summary: Lionel Messi could not conjure up one final piece of brilliance on a dismal afternoon for Argentina who ended the World Cup final in defeat and disgrace
articles.content:
Lionel Messi: Time to leave the international scene but remember the good times, not the shame of New Jersey

Lionel Messi could not conjure up one final piece of brilliance on a dismal afternoon for Argentina who ended the World Cup final in defeat and disgrace

Last Update:

Lionel Messi stood staring at the Argentina fans, tears streaming down his face.

Behind him, Spain were lifting the World Cup following a victory that was a triumph for quality, persistence and restraint.

The fact Messi and his team-mates did not turn round and watch the victors lift the trophy came as no surprise; it was merely a continuation of a classless attitude evident from the outset.

Their sole gameplan was to frustrate and cheat, using thuggish tactics in the hope it took them to a penalty shoot-out. Mercifully, for the game of football it did not succeed.

The antics of Leandro Paredes, who should have earlier joined Enzo Fernández in being sent-off, and Nahuel Molina at the final whistle, throwing punches at Spain players as they celebrated summed up a team that knew they had been handed a footballing lesson.

Argentina did not have a shot of any description until the 117th minute. That came from Messi on one of the few occasions he managed to escape the iron fist of Spain’s control.

Table of Contents

Messi’s final let-down after another brilliant World Cup

Messi, as always, had been Argentina’s star man throughout a tournament during which he turned 39 years of age. But he was a largely peripheral figure as Spain dominated the ball in a one-sided encounter. The Inter Miami star managed just 54 touches in 120 minutes and spent much of the afternoon trotting around as the European champions pinged the ball from one player to another.

As he did in Argentina’s successful 2022 campaign in Qatar, Messi dragged a collection of moderately talented players to the final with eight goals and providing the inspiration for many more.

But not even he could influence a fight as one-sided as this though and his obvious irritation spilled over in the second half of normal time as he attempted to get Marc Cucurella sent off for covering his mouth, waving his hand towards the sidelines like a child attempting to get the teacher’s attention. It was unbecoming of the eight-time Ballon d’Or winner and a desperate act of a man who knew his team were in need of help.

That it didn’t come was also a slight surprise. The widespread accusations that Argentina were given preferential treatment by referees may be misplaced but they were certainly on the right side of several key decisions throughout the tournament.

Slovenian official Slavko Vincic attempted to let the final flow but it was a nigh on impossible task due to Argentina’s persistent infractions with the only criticism being he ought to have clamped down on them earlier.

If he had then Messi and Co would undoubtedly have suffered a deserved defeat in 90 minutes, rather than having to wait until 106 for Ferran Torres to finally apply the killer touch.

Messi likely to walk away after fantastic international career

Given his age and the fact this appears the end of a cycle for Argentina with several ageing players, and coach Lionel Scaloni, set to walk away, it seems highly likely Messi’s international career is now over.

It is perhaps fitting it will end at the same MetLife Stadium where he announced his international retirement in 2016 after a Copa America final defeat to Chile, their fourth final defeat in nine years.

Having been persuaded to carry on, Messi returned with a bang, perhaps not initially as a disjointed side failed to make much of an impression in Russia in 2018, but his moment was to come three years later with victory at the Copa America.

Argentina backed that up by lifting the trophy in Qatar – their first world crown in 36 years – before another Copa win in 2024.

Messi was the driving force behind them all and it is only right to focus on those successes rather than dwell on the angry, bitter, miserable performance against Spain.

Only Messi knows what the tears represented at the final whistle. Disappointment, regret, perhaps even a little embarrassment at being caught up in Argentina’s shameful approach in New Jersey.

In the end, it doesn’t really matter. Messi will now disappear once and for all from the biggest stage and spend his final months, or years, torturing defences in Major League Soccer.

Thank you for the memories, it’s just a shame it had to end this way.

articles.title: Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni likely to leave in December following World Cup heartbreak
articles.summary: Argentina's World Cup-winning boss Lionel Scaloni says he will most likely walk away in December when his contract expires
articles.content:
Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni likely to leave in December following World Cup heartbreak

Argentina's World Cup-winning boss Lionel Scaloni says he will most likely walk away in December when his contract expires

Last Update:

Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni has confirmed he will probably leave the post when his contract expires in December.

Scaloni took over in 2018 and has enjoyed a golden period in charge, leading his country to two Copas America and the World Cup title in 2022. However, the team’s attempts to win a second world crown ended in disappointment and disgrace in New Jersey last night with a dreadful performance against Spain – they didn’t register a shot until the 27th minute of extra-time – as the European champions won 1-0.

Argentina’s gameplan was to frustrate and they used all the dark arts to achieve it with Enzo Fernandez sent off in the second half of normal time. Their frustration spilled over after the final whistle when Leandro Paredes and Nahuel Molina started brawling with Spain players as they celebrated.

Despite bizarrely claiming his players know how to lose gracefully, Scaloni deserves huge credit for enabling a fairly limited side to reach the final once again.

He broke down in tears at the official post-match press conference when discussing his future and confirmed in the mixed zone that he was set to depart at the end of the year.

I’ll probably stop, says Argentina boss Scaloni

He said: “I’ll be here until December, and then I’ll probably stop.

“Honestly, I feel the need to think because I don’t know if we’ll be able to do something as grand as this. We would need to talk. I am grateful to the president of AFA for giving me this opportunity. To be in a place that I am in, which is a dream for everyone. We tried until the last minute to give it our all, the coaching staff and players. I think it’s just that I take the time to think.

“This place is marvellous. To continue, we need a lot of things. We need to reset. We need to form a group like this one, which is difficult to form again. It hurts my soul. I’m sorry.”

It is likely to be a period of change for Argentina with several ageing players coming towards the end of their international careers, most notably Lionel Messi.

articles.title: ‘We know how to lose’ – Scaloni humble in defeat as Argentina fail to defend World Cup title
articles.summary: Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni says his side know how to lose after heartbreak in the World Cup final.
articles.content:
‘We know how to lose’ – Scaloni humble in defeat as Argentina fail to defend World Cup title

Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni says his side know how to lose after heartbreak in the World Cup final.

Last Update:

Lionel Scaloni paid tribute to his players and accepted Spain were worthy winners after Argentina’s bid to defend the World Cup title ended in a 1-0 defeat after extra time at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey.

Ferran Torres scored the only goal of the final in the 106th minute, converting from close range after Nico Williams’ cross had found Mikel Merino at the back post.

Argentina had survived 90 minutes thanks to an extraordinary display from Emiliano Martinez, who made 11 saves to break the World Cup final record and keep Spain at bay.

Argentina did not register a single shot in normal time, the first team in history to achieve that unwanted distinction in a World Cup final, but they resisted to the very end before Enzo Fernandez’s second yellow card in the 90th minute reduced them to ten men and ultimately opened the door for Torres to settle it.

Scaloni, who has managed Argentina since 2018 and overseen a golden era that delivered the 2021 Copa America, the 2022 World Cup and the 2024 Copa America, was gracious in defeat.

“I feel sad but I am aware that we played our hearts out. There are many things I would like to say, but I can’t really. I am forever thankful to these guys who have competed all the way,” he said.

“They were better to be honest. I have really fond memories of what they did and how difficult it is to get here.

“We need to attach a great deal of value to what we have done. We are big in victory and we must be big in defeat. Today we showed that we know how to lose.

“We lost the game and we accept that. But it doesn’t mean that we will forget everything we have done so far. I would like to tell the country that we played our hearts out.”

Messi’s farewell

The defeat almost certainly marks the end of Lionel Messi’s World Cup career.

The 39-year-old, playing his sixth and final tournament, was kept quiet throughout the final by a Spain side that afforded him almost nothing.

He finished without a shot on target, a stark contrast to a tournament in which he had broken Miroslav Klose’s all-time World Cup scoring record and become the first player in history to score or assist in 11 consecutive World Cup matches.

Spain’s combination of Pau Cubarsi and Aymeric Laporte at centre-back, sitting behind a world-class midfield, denied Messi the pockets of space that had defined his tournament up to that point.

He gave the ball away more than any other Argentina player on the night, a first in a 2026 campaign that had produced moments of brilliance that will outlast the result.

articles.summary: Ferran Torres gave Spain victory over Argentina in the World Cup final 2026
articles.content:
Ferran Torres confesses Lionel Messi ‘nervousness’ before World Cup final 2026: ‘The goal belonged to 47 million’

Ferran Torres gave Spain victory over Argentina in the World Cup final 2026

Last Update:

Ferran Torres says his goal “belonged to 47 million people” in Spain after La Roja overcame their anxiety about facing Lionel Messi to win the World Cup final 2026.

Barcelona’s Torres struck in the 106th minute in New Jersey to ensure 39-year-old Messi failed to win a second successive World Cup title in what could prove the icon’s last international match.

“Destiny was written,” substitute Torres said, via AS. “We were made to win.

“If all finals are difficult, when you have Messi as an opponent, that nervousness sets in. We [played] more football.”

Table of Contents

World Cup final 2026: Spain beat Argentina

In a tempestuous encounter, Argentina had Enzo Fernandez dismissed during added time in the second half of regular time.

“In the end, the goal belonged to 47 million people, not just to me out of 26 [Spain players],” said 26-year-old Torres.

“[It’s] a huge relief. I’ve been heavily criticised during the World Cup. Thank God, who always gives me the strength to keep going.”

World Cup final 2026: Spain team vs Argentina

Spain were unchanged from their semi-final win over France, bringing Torres on for Mikel Oyarzabal in the 62nd minute.

Spain starting XI: Unai Simon, Pedro Porro, Pau Cubarsi, Aymeric Laporte, Marc Cucurella, Rodri, Fabian Ruiz, Lamine Yamal, Dani Olmo, Alex Baena, Mikel Oyarzabal

Spain substitutes: David Raya, Joan Garcia, Marc Pubill, Alex Grimaldo, Eric Garcia, Marcos Llorente, Mikel Merino, Gavi, Martin Zubimendi, Pedri, Ferran Torres, Yeremy Pino, Nico Williams, Victor Munoz, Borja Iglesias

World Cup final 2026: Argentina full starting line up vs Spain

Argentina made three alterations from their last-four victory over England, bringing in Rodrigo De Paul, Nico Gonzalez and Gonzalo Montiel for Giuliano Simeone, Leandro Paredes and Nahuel Molina.

Argentina XI: Emiliano Martinez, Nicolas Tagliafico, Gonzalo Montiel, Lisandro Martinez, Cristian Romero, Rodrigo De Paul, Nico Gonzalez, Alexis Mac Allister, Enzo Fernandez, Julian Alvarez, Lionel Messi

Argentina substitutes: Juan Musso, Geronimo Rulli, Marcos Senesi, Nicolas Otamendi, Facundo Medina, Nahuel Molina, Leandro Paredes, Valentin Barco, Giovani Lo Celso, Exequiel Palacios, Thiago Almada, Giuliano Simeone, Nico Paz, Jose Manuel Lopez, Lautaro Martinez

articles.title: What time is the World Cup final 2026 halftime show? Shakira, Madonna, Justin Bieber, BTS confirmed start time and where to watch full show on TV and live online stream
articles.summary: The lowdown on the World Cup 2026 final and half-time show
articles.content:
What time is the World Cup final 2026 halftime show? Shakira, Madonna, Justin Bieber, BTS confirmed start time and where to watch full show on TV and live online stream

The lowdown on the World Cup 2026 final and half-time show

Last Update:

Spain, Argentina and a gaggle of pop stars will attempt to make the 104th and final match of the World Cup 2026 a spectacle to remember on Sunday.

Eight-time Ballon d’Or winner Lionel Messi is hoping to inspire the holders and finish as the tournament top scorer.

La Roja’s ranks include 19-year-old sensation Lamine Yamal and former Ballon d’Or winner Rodri, with the performers on the pitch set for an extended half-time break while music takes centre stage in New Jersey.

Justin Bieber will co-headline alongside Madonna, Shakira and K-pop (or Korean pop) boy band BTS in a ceremony FIFA say will combine “football, music and social impact”.

Table of Contents

What time is the World Cup final 2026?

The match kicks off at 20:00 BST on Sunday, July 19. Here’s how that translates in different territories.

Where is the World Cup final 2026?

The game will take place at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, which has a capacity of almost 81,000.

The spectacular setting is the home of NFL teams the New York Giants and the New York Jets and will host its eighth match at the finals, averaging more than three goals per game.

Contests held at the venue have included record five-time champions Brazil’s group-stage draw with Morocco and quarter-final defeat to Norway.

France beat Sweden and Senegal at the MetLife Stadium, which was the stage for Ecuador’s surprise win over four-time champions Germany during the group phase.

What time is the halftime show at the World Cup 2026?

Assuming there are no weather delays, the half-time show should start shortly after the end of the first half. Here are the earliest times it could start.

World Cup 2026 halftime show: Who is playing?

Pop megastar Shakira is partly responsible for the official World Cup 2026 song, Dai Dai, and will be joined by colossally popular Nigerian singer Burna Boy, her collaborator on the record.

This is the first time a half-time show has taken place during a World Cup final and the ceremony has been arranged by English band and familiar American stadium fillers Coldplay.

BTS will be back at the MetLife Stadium in August for two dates as part of their US tour. “They’ll be part of a moment that reaches far beyond the pitch,” half-time show producers Global Citizen promised of the performance.

Earlier this week, BTS’ new single, Normal, became the most-streamed K-Pop music video in a single day on the platform.

Rodri claims Spain must play ‘without fear’ ahead  of World Cup final

Rodri has revealed the blueprint for Spain to beat Argentina toniight.

Last Update:

Spain captain Rodri says reaching the World Cup final is the result of years of progress and believes his side must play without fear when they face defending champions Argentina on Sunday.

Spain are preparing for only the second World Cup final in the nation’s history after building on their recent international success, having won the Nations League in 2023 and Euro 2024.

Rodri believes those achievements laid the foundations for the team’s current run and says Spain have grown stronger over the past five years.

“We’ve been gradually growing,” he said.

“We have to keep doing the same things we’re doing because it has been a process for all five years.”

Spain have impressed throughout the tournament, conceding just one goal in seven matches.

After opening with a surprise draw against Cape Verde, they have won six straight games, including a 2-0 semi-final win over France, while outscoring opponents 13-1.

“Our goal when we got to this World Cup was to win the trophy, and we were convinced that we could achieve this,” Rodri said.

“We’ve shown that this national team has been able to defeat great opponents.”

Table of Contents

Rodri: Spain can be unpredictable

Rodri rejected the suggestion that Spain only have one way of playing, insisting they can adapt to whatever challenge Argentina present.

“I don’t think you’ve seen the same Spain across all the matches,” he said.

“I think Sunday’s match will be quite different because it will be more physical and we must be prepared.

“If we are known for something in this national team, it’s that we know how to play different games based on the moment.

“We can adapt to defending, counter-attacking or attacking. We are a very complete team, and that is why we are here.”

Although Spain’s 2010 World Cup-winning side remains an inspiration, Rodri believes this group can still improve.

“We can even do it better,” he said.

“I think against France we played one of the best games we’ve ever played as a team. But against Argentina, we have to raise our level because they are the champions. I’m really confident that we can do it.”

Yamal ready for World Cup final

There had been concern over Lamine Yamal after the 19-year-old was seen in training with his left thigh heavily strapped following a knock against France.

Spain head coach Luis de la Fuente dismissed any fitness concerns ahead of the final.

“Today he trained with the rest of the squad and he is fine,” De la Fuente said.

“He is fine. He is in optimal condition.”

Yamal, who was famously photographed alongside Lionel Messi as a baby in 2007, has been tipped by many as the Argentine’s eventual successor, but De la Fuente wants the Barcelona winger to focus on being himself.

“Lamine has to be Lamine,” he said.

“Messi is a once-in-history player. He’s an example for young players because of his attitude and behaviour.

“I insist Lamine has to be Lamine Yamal himself. The best way we can support him is by helping him continue to be the person we know today because he has enormous potential and a great future.”

articles.summary: Messi has eight goals going into the final
articles.content:
World Cup 2026: How Messi can win the Golden Boot

Messi has eight goals going into the final

Last Update:

Lionel Messi has won just about everything in the game, but the elusive World Cup Golden Boot remains in his sights on final day.

Heading into Sunday’s World Cup final against Spain at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, the Argentina superstar finds himself chasing down a familiar foe. Thanks to a wild, 10-goal third-place play-off on Saturday, France’s Kylian Mbappé has thrown down the gauntlet by storming to the top of the goalscoring charts.

To snatch the trophy from Mbappé’s grasp, Messi- who sits two goals behind – must produce a vintage masterclass in the final. Because Messi has one more assist than the Frenchman, a spectacular hat-trick would win it outright, while a brace would pull him level on goals and potentially secure the award via that assist advantage.

Even if the 39-year-old icon falls short of the goalscoring crown, a record-extending third Golden Ball as the tournament’s best player seems well within reach. He is already the only player to win the award multiple times since its 1978 inception (in 2014 and 2022), and sparking Argentina’s run to a second straight final at his age gives him an undeniable case.

“He is the history. He is the legend,” Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said.

Table of Contents

The Golden Boot Race: How the Leaderboard Looks

Mbappé’s double in France’s chaotic 6-4 defeat to England made him the first player to hit double digits at a single World Cup since German legend Gerd Müller in 1970.

Here is how the top of the leaderboard shapes up ahead of Sunday’s final:

Kylian Mbappé (France) – 10 Goals (4 Assists)

Lionel Messi (Argentina) – 8 Goals (4 Assists)

Jude Bellingham (England) – 7 Goals (1 Assist)

Erling Haaland (Norway) – 7 Goals (0 Assists)

Ousmane Dembélé (France) – 6 Goals (2 Assists)

Harry Kane (England) – 6 Goals (1 Assist)

Mikel Oyarzabal (Spain) – 5 Goals (1 Assist)

Should Messi score the necessary goals to overtake Mbappé and anchor an Argentina victory, he would become the first Golden Boot winner to play for the tournament champions since Brazil’s Ronaldo netted eight times in 2002.

A Clean Sweep of Silverware on the Line

The final will also decide the remaining individual accolades, voted on by the media and FIFA’s Technical Study Group. Spain is in a fantastic position to dominate the podium alongside their team ambitions.

La Roja’s goalkeeper Unai Simón is a heavy favourite for the Golden Glove after an incredible tournament which has included breaking the historic World Cup record for consecutive minutes without conceding. Meanwhile, Spain’s 19-year-old sensation Lamine Yamal has provided endless dazzle up front, making him the undisputed frontrunner for the Best Young Player Award.

articles.title: England should be proud of third place says Tuchel after crazy France win
articles.summary: England had their best World Cup since 1966
articles.content:
England should be proud of third place says Tuchel after crazy France win

England had their best World Cup since 1966

Last Update:

England manager Thomas Tuchel hopes his players will one day look back on finishing third at the World Cup with some pride, despite falling short of their ultimate goal of winning the tournament.

A sensational 6-4 victory over France in a frenetic third-place playoff at Miami Stadium on Saturday secured England their best finish at a World Cup since their legendary 1966 triumph on home soil.

Despite the historic feat, the heartbreak of missing out on the final still lingered for the German manager – and fans.

“It’s the first medal for 60 years, the best World Cup on foreign soil. So I hope that the players can be proud of that in some time,” Tuchel said.

“We are fiercely competitive, so like we almost don’t allow ourselves to be proud of the third place because 18 months ago we set ourselves the highest goal, to make it to the final and win the World Cup.

“So it’s very, very painful if you miss out. The pain will stay for a while.”

Tuchel Hits Back at Critics After Semi-Final Flak

Tuchel came in for heavy criticism after England lost 2-1 to Argentina in the semi-finals on Wednesday. The manager faced intense scrutiny, particularly because of what were viewed as his defensive tactics after his side took the lead early in the second half.

Addressing the intense media pressure, the Three Lions boss didn’t hold back regarding the atmosphere surrounding the squad ahead of the France clash.

“The press conference yesterday felt as if we went out in the group stage without a win, to be very honest,” the German said.

“The best thing you can do is react on the pitch and get the next win. Everything else is just talking, and talking doesn’t get you points, and talking doesn’t get you a win.

“I’m glad that we showed a reaction. We wanted that reaction, and it’s very impressive.”

Bukayo Saka’s stunning hat-trick against France inevitably raised a burning question: why was the Arsenal right winger left out of the crucial semi-final clash against Argentina?

Tuchel admitted he had been cautious with Saka due to a lingering Achilles injury the forward had been managing for the last few months, but defended his tactical gamble on the night.

“It was a tough decision for me to leave him out of the semi-final,” said Tuchel. “I had the feeling that Morgan Rogers had something special to give to us with his physicality and his body in the match against Argentina.

“We had (Saka) warm up several times against Argentina. We were ready to change, but the game became so crazy that we in the end opted for a different option.

“But nothing has changed during the World Cup for me. Bukayo is a fantastic teammate, fantastic football player, key player for us, and that will not change. He showed it again today and I’m happy for him.”

articles.summary: France coach leaves the stage after another classic game
articles.content:
End of an Era: Didier Deschamps bows out in chaos as England edge 10-Goal World Cup thriller

France coach leaves the stage after another classic game

Last Update:

An extraordinary 14-year reign came to a dramatic and painful end in Miami on Saturday night.

Didier Deschamps’ legendary tenure as France national team coach concluded in one of the most chaotic matches in recent World Cup history, with Les Bleus suffering a 6-4 defeat to England in the third-place playoff.

The match provided none of the controlled, disciplined football that came to define much of Deschamps’ tenure. Instead, France found themselves trailing 4-0 at half-time after a catastrophic opening 45 minutes. While they mounted a spirited second-half recovery, the late rally wasn’t enough to save Deschamps’ 185th and final match in charge from ending in defeat.

Following the final whistle, Deschamps took full responsibility for the first-half horror show.

“It is a defeat, but we were 4-0 down. We produced an unacceptable first half,” Deschamps said.

“There was a reaction, with the things we know how to do well. We had two chances to make it 4-4, but we pushed forward a little more.

“That is what we know how to do, but we didn’t do it. It is my fault because I must not have done what was needed in the first half.”

France arrived at the tournament with high hopes of capturing a third world title, but their campaign derailed in the final week. A 2-0 semi-final defeat to Spain shattered their dreams of reaching a third successive World Cup final, before England inflicted one last setback on the outgoing boss.

Deschamps admitted the sporting disappointment remained considerable, even if the second-half fightback restored some pride.

“It would have been better to finish third,” he said. “We came here with a lot of ambition. We managed to do quite a few positive things.

“We failed in our match against Spain and they knew how to perform against us. This is a group with footballing quality. There was enough talent to get results.

“On a human level, it was a beautiful adventure. Eight weeks, it was beautiful.

“The disappointment is there on a sporting level. We had the opportunity to create emotions for tens of millions of French people. It is the World Cup, there is nothing more beautiful.”

France pays tribute to a dominant force

Despite the chaotic nature of his final match, nothing can diminish a legacy that transformed France into the most consistent powerhouse of the modern era. Shortly after the game, the French Football Federation (FFF) paid a glowing tribute to the departing icon, who leaves his post after 187 matches and 122 victories.

“Didier Deschamps embodied high standards, rigour, a sense of the collective and love for the blue shirt,” the FFF said in an official statement.

“Under his leadership, for 14 years, the France team regained credibility, respect and affection while remaining at the highest level in the world.”

Deschamps leaves the international stage as a true titan of the game. He famously captained France to their first World Cup triumph in 1998 and won the European Championship two years later.

By guiding Les Bleus to glory in Russia, he became one of only three men in football history to win the World Cup as both a player and a coach. Alongside the 2018 crown, he led France to the 2021 Nations League title, as well as the finals of Euro 2016 and the 2022 World Cup.
